one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 2026 results are reported for about Nov 11, 2026 (third-party calendar, not yet confirmed by the company; last year's Q3 came Nov 5), and the class-action lead-plaintiff deadline is Nov 16. Both fall after Oct 31. What does fall inside the window is a stream of alternative-data reads: weekly Pixel-install and merchant-count trackers (Citi, Wells Fargo), app-ad share data, and pre-earnings previews. Recent prints have moved the stock 3-5% a day (Wells Fargo's 'false start' note on Sep 30). These cut both ways, and the stock sits at a fresh 52-week low after a 60% drawdown, where momentum and short-term reversal roughly offset each other. So I stay symmetric around $281.31 with a monthly sigma of about 20% (75% annual realized vol / 3.5 is about 21%) and take no directional view.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (haircut FY27 EPS $18.5 x 18x = $333), EV/EBITDA (FY27 EBITDA ~$7.9B x 12x, net debt $0.46B, 330M shares = $287) and FCF yield (FY27 FCF ~$6.0B at a 6.5% yield = $280), weighted 40/30/30, gives about $302.

inputs_detail.value: $20.00 (27 analysts; $21.16 sixty days ago; 19 down vs 5 up revisions in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: I cut consensus by 7.5%. Revisions are still falling, and the alternative data (Wells Fargo traffic-weighted Pixel data, a weak raw merchant ramp) points to e-commerce becoming a 2027 story rather than a 2026 one, so the e-commerce ramp built into 2027 consensus looks too early.

The market today pays about 14x FY27 consensus ($281/$20). The growth outlook is still about 25-30% (FY27 revenue $10.26B vs FY26 $8.10B), there is no balance-sheet stress, and the SEC probe was closed. Against that, the AI-model execution miss, the class action and a sentiment de-rating cap the multiple well below the 30x+ history. I use 18x, roughly in line with large-cap ad peers.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY2027 adj. EBITDA ~$7.9B (revenue $9.8B x 81%) x 12x, less $0.46B net debt, / 330M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus less about 4.5% for a slower e-commerce ramp, per Wells Fargo's Pixel-quality work and the AI video-tool delay.
Q2 2026 margin was 84% and Q3 guidance is 83%; I take a little off for investment in creative tools and self-serve.

Today's EV (about $95B at $281 x 337M diluted shares plus $0.46B net debt) over annualized Q3-guide EBITDA ($1.725B x 4 = $6.9B) is about 13.8x. A slightly lower multiple on forward EBITDA reflects the de-rating.
337.0M diluted in Q2, less about 2% net buyback over 12 months (Q2 repurchase $551M; 1.1M shares).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY2027 FCF ~$6.0B at a 6.5% yield, / 330M shares (plus net debt adjustment)

inputs_detail.derivation: Net income of about $18.5 x 335M = $6.2B, converted at about 97% to FCF. Q2 FCF of $863M was depressed by timing against $1.27B of net income, so conversion is uncertain.
TIKR puts the NTM levered FCF yield at about 6% today (vs about 2% at end-2025). I require slightly more given the execution and legal overhang.

bear.story: The e-commerce/web self-serve push stalls, as the traffic-weighted Pixel data suggests: most new sites are dormant APAC storefronts, and the Muddy Waters incrementality critique sticks. Model gains stay lumpy, and Unity Vector, Mintegral and Meta's AI game tools chip at gaming share. FY27 EPS comes in around $15 and the multiple compresses to about 11x.

base.story: Gaming stays dominant (about 36% of mobile game ad revenue, rising on iOS). The model upgrades put in place after Q2 bring growth back toward guidance, and e-commerce scales slowly through 2027. FY27 EPS is about $18.5-19 and the market keeps a mid-to-high-teens multiple while the class action lingers.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 beat on model improvements, the generative video tool ships, and Jefferies-style survey share gains (11.1% of DTC budgets) turn into real web revenue. Consensus FY27 EPS of $20+ holds or rises and the stock re-rates toward 22-24x, about the Street's ~$498 mean target.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $175 (under 9x FY27 consensus EPS and roughly a 10% FCF yield), the price would most likely mean the earnings base itself is breaking, not just the multiple. That would look like a guide-down implying negative sequential growth in the core gaming business, evidence of share loss to Unity Vector or Meta, platform or deplatforming action tied to data practices, or e-commerce cohorts churning. The fall from $738 to $281 can be explained by de-rating plus a modest growth reset; a further 38% drop cannot without a fundamental problem.

key_uncertainties: Whether e-commerce/web adoption is real: raw Pixel installs spiked to 750 and then 1,600 a week, but about 85% of new sites have no measurable traffic
Cadence of Axon model improvements after the Q2 'lighter model improvements' miss
Gaming share durability against Unity Vector, Mintegral and AdMob, and AI game-creation tools from Meta
Securities class action outcome and any renewed regulatory or platform scrutiny of data practices (the SEC probe itself was closed with no action)
FCF conversion: Q2 FCF $863M vs net income $1.27B
Sentiment and momentum: the stock fell from $738 to $281 with downward estimate revisions still coming in
reasoning: Hard facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $1.92B (+53% y/y) with an 84% EBITDA margin, just below guidance, and Q3 is guided to $2.055-2.085B. Net debt is about $0.46B and diluted shares about 337M. The stock fell from $738 to $281 on a BofA e-commerce note (Jul 13, -12.6%), the Q2 miss tied to the AI video-tool delay (Aug 6, -19.6%), a class action, and the Sep 30 Wells Fargo Pixel note. In my lane, the alternative data is mixed. Bearish: the traffic-weighted Pixel data says the late-September install spike was mostly dormant APAC Shopify stores, from an install base of about 6,000 sites vs Snap at 118k and Pinterest at 489k, so web revenue looks like a 2027 story. Bullish: Sensor Tower data shows APP's share of mobile game ad revenue still rising (about 36% overall, iOS up from 39% to 44% in Q2 2026). A Jefferies survey of 30 DTC advertisers shows budget share rising 169bp to 11.1%, with APP ranking top-3 on ROAS. Practitioner write-ups say model upgrades shipped after Q2 and consumer spend was a record. The SEC probe closed with no action. No prediction market lists the name (searched Polymarket and Kalshi). X/Reddit was not reached directly; social-sourced claims were used only where a second source confirmed them. At about 14x FY27 consensus EPS ($20), the stock prices in a lot of skepticism. My haircut fair value is about $302, a little above spot, with downside skew from still-falling revisions. I use a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $165/25%, base $305/50%, bull $470/25%, inner sigmas 25-35%), which gives a total spread consistent with roughly 60-70% annual vol, a bit below the 75% realized figure that includes two crash days. That puts P(>=281) at about 0.56 and the median near $300. Research was limited to about 14 searches and fetches; Benzinga blocked fetching.
